measures.group: Reforming welfare to get Britain working

measures.group: Reforming welfare to get Britain working

measures.group: Reforming welfare to get Britain working

measures.name: Universal Credit Health Element: Maintain at 2025-26 rate until 2029-30, reduce rate by 50% for new claimants from April 2026 and maintain until 2029-30
measures.group: Reforming welfare to get Britain working

measures.name: Universal Credit Standard Allowance: Increase above inflation for all claimants from April 2026, reaching CPI +5% from April 2029, with the standard allowance expected to be worth £106 per week in 2029-30
measures.group: Reforming welfare to get Britain working

measures.name: Welfare Fraud and Error: Increase preventative checks in Universal Credit from 2025-26
measures.group: Reforming welfare to get Britain working

measures.name: Welfare Fraud and Error: Recruit over 500 new counter fraud and error staff from April 2025
measures.group: Reforming welfare to get Britain working

measures.name: Tax Debt Collection: Invest in additional HMRC debt management capacity to increase collection of overdue tax debt
Tax Debt Collection: Invest in 600 additional HMRC debt management staff to increase collection of overdue tax debt
Tax Collection: Invest in 500 additional HMRC compliance staff to increase collection of tax due
Late Payment Penalties: Increase late payment penalties for VAT taxpayers and income tax Self Assessment taxpayers as they join Making Tax Digital from April 2025
Making Tax Digital for income tax Self Assessment: Expand rollout to those with incomes over £20,000 from 6 April 2028, and further detailed changes
Building Safety Levy: Implement a levy on new residential development in England (with certain exemptions) with revenue to be spent on building safety from 1 October 2026
Gambling: New statutory levy on operators from April 2025
Gambling: Use new levy revenue to fund research, prevention, and treatment of gambling-related harm

UK Export Finance: Fees/income from increasing lending capacity and providing guarantees for defence exports (only fees & interest impact shown as loans & guarantees do not affect public sector net borrowing)
Support for Local Government: Net impact of pre-announced support for local government via capitalisation directions, and council tax/fire & police precept flexibilities
Parental leave: Increase the small employer compensation rate to 8.5% from April 2025 following National Insurance changes at Autumn Budget 2024
Reducing Trade Barriers: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) tariff liberalisation
Reducing Trade Barriers: Approve UK business applications for removal of tariff duty on 89 products for 2 years from Spring 2025
High Income Child Benefit Charge (HICBC): Allow employed individuals to pay their HICBC liability through PAYE without the need to register for Self Assessment from Summer 2025

Supplementary Estimates: CDEL Supplementary Estimates Plans for 2024-25
